newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen and Canada's Calvalley sign oil exploration.
newsitem.headline: Yemen and Canada's Calvalley sign oil exploration.

text.p: Yemen and Canada's Calvalley Petroleum Inc signed an oil exploration deal on Sunday, state-run television said.
Officials of the Calgary-based firm and Yemen's Oil and Mineral Resources Ministry signed the oil concession covering sector nine between Yemen's Shabwa and Hadramout provinces.
It is located between a producing field operated by Canadian Occidental Petroleum Ltd, one of Yemen's most prominent foreign investors, and another operated by France's Total SA.
Yemeni television gave no further details. Government and company officials were not immediately available for comment.
Calvalley said two months ago it signed a memorandum of understanding with Yemen to explore two sectors totalling 15,000 square km.
The area covered by the MOUs includes sector nine and sector 39 in Mahra province, Ed Shimoon, the company's president, told Reuters in December.
Yemeni media did not refer to the MOU part dealing with sector 39, located on once-disputed land on the Yemen-Oman border, which is now under Yemeni control.
Phillips Petroleum P.A operates an exploration concession in Oman, across the border from the Calvalley lands, Shimoon said.
The blocks currently produce no oil, although seismic data covering some of the acreage exists, Shimoon said.
The agreement would allow Calvalley to explore on the lands for a six-year term.
State-run media also said Yemen's oil ministry and Hungary's oil and gas company Magyar Olaj- es Gazipari Rt (MOL) signed a MOU on Sunday to explore oil in sector 49 in Hadramout.
Last July, MOL joined a consortium with U.S.'s Occidental and Amerada Hess to look for oil in block Uqlah S-2 in the Yemeni desert.
Occidental has a 50 percent share in the consortium, while Amerada has 30 and MOL 20 percent.
